source.title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems

accepted.question_text: For every Tychonoff topological space X, does there exist an R-quotient mapping from X onto an infinite subspace of the closed unit interval [0,1], where an R-quotient mapping phi: X -> Y is a surjective continuous map such that, for every real-valued function f on Y, f composed with phi is continuous if and only if f is continuous?

evidence.quote: A surjective continuous mapping phi :X->Y is said to be R-quotient [14] if for every real-valued function f on Y, the composition f o phi is continuous if and only if f is continuous.
Does there exist an R-quotient mapping from each Tychonoff space onto an infinite subspace of [0,1]?

accepted.question_text: For every Lindelof topological space X, does there exist an R-quotient mapping from X onto an infinite separable Tychonoff space?

evidence.quote: Does there exist an R-quotient mapping from each Lindelof space onto an infinite separable Tychonoff space?

accepted.question_text: Let C be a class of separable topological groups and let V(C) be the variety generated by C, meaning the intersection of all nonempty classes of topological groups containing C that are closed under taking subgroups, quotient groups, arbitrary cartesian products, and isomorphic images. If the groups in C are not assumed to be abelian, must every metrizable group in V(C) be separable?

evidence.quote: Recall that a non-empty class of topological groups is said to be a variety if it is closed under the operations of taking subgroups, quotient groups, (arbitrary) cartesian products and isomorphic images.
Does Corollary 5 remain valid if we drop the assumption that all groups in the class C are abelian?

accepted.question_text: In ZFC alone, does there exist a separable countably compact topological group that contains a non-separable closed subgroup?

evidence.quote: Does there exist in ZFC a separable countably compact topological group which contains a non-separable closed subgroup?

accepted.question_text: Characterize the frontier of S-separable topological groups, where a topological group G is S-separable if, for every topological group H whose closed subgroups are all separable, every closed subgroup of G x H is separable. In particular: is every separable locally compact group S-separable; is the additive group of real numbers with its Euclidean topology S-separable; does there exist a separable metrizable group that is not S-separable; and is the free topological group on the closed unit interval [0,1] S-separable?

evidence.quote: Let us say that a topological group G is strongly separable (briefly, S-separable) if for any topological group H such that every closed subgroup of H is separable, the product G x H has each of its closed subgroups separable.
Find the frontiers of the class of S-separable topological groups.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a countably compact topological group such that every closed subgroup of G is separable, and let H be a topological group with a countable network. Must every closed subgroup of the product group G x H be separable?

evidence.quote: Let G be a countably compact topological group such that all closed subgroups of G are separable, and H a topological group with a countable network. Are the closed subgroups of G x H separable?

accepted.question_text: Let S be the smallest class of topological groups generated by all compact separable groups and all countable groups and closed under finite products, taking closed subgroups, and taking continuous homomorphic images. Is a topological group G in S if and only if G contains a compact separable subgroup K such that the quotient space G/K is countable?

evidence.quote: Does a topological group G belong to the class S if and only if G contains a compact separable subgroup K such that the quotient space G/K is countable?

accepted.question_text: Can the following two consistency-dependent existence results be proved in ZFC alone: first, that there exist pseudocompact abelian topological groups G and H such that every closed subgroup of G and of H is separable but G x H contains a closed non-separable sigma-compact subgroup; and second, that there exist pseudocomplete locally convex spaces K and L such that every closed vector subspace of K and of L is separable but K x L contains a closed non-separable sigma-compact vector subspace?

evidence.quote: Assume that 2^{omega_1}=c. Then there exist pseudocompact abelian topological groups G and H such that all closed subgroups of G and H are separable, but the product G x H contains a closed non-separable sigma-compact subgroup.
Are Theorems 16 and 19 valid in ZFC alone?

accepted.question_text: Characterize the Tychonoff spaces X for which every closed vector subspace of C_p(X) is separable, where C_p(X) denotes the space of all continuous real-valued functions on X endowed with the topology of pointwise convergence.

evidence.quote: Let C_p(X,E) denote the space of all continuous E-valued functions on X endowed with the pointwise convergence topology.
Characterize those Tychonoff spaces X such that all closed vector subspaces of C_p(X) are separable.

accepted.question_text: If K is an arbitrary separable Banach space and L is a topological vector space whose closed vector subspaces are all separable, must every closed vector subspace of the product K x L be separable? This asks whether the known finite-dimensional version, proved when K is finite-dimensional, extends to all separable Banach spaces K.

evidence.quote: It is not known whether Proposition 9 remains valid for an arbitrary separable Banach space K.

accepted.question_text: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have a quotient Banach space that is both separable and infinite-dimensional?

evidence.quote: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have a quotient Banach space which is separable and infinite-dimensional?

accepted.question_text: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a quotient group that is non-trivial and separable?

evidence.quote: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a quotient group which is a non-trivial separable topological group?

accepted.question_text: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a quotient group that is infinite and separable?

evidence.quote: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a quotient group which is an infinite separable topological group?

accepted.question_text: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a quotient group that is non-trivial, separable, and metrizable?

evidence.quote: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a quotient group which is a non-trivial separable metrizable topological group?

accepted.question_text: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a quotient group that is infinite, separable, and metrizable?

evidence.quote: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a quotient group which is an infinite separable metrizable topological group?

accepted.question_text: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space, viewed as an additive topological group, have a quotient group whose underlying topological space is homeomorphic to the countable product R^omega of real lines?

evidence.quote: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have a quotient group which is homeomorphic to R^omega?

accepted.question_text: For every infinite locally compact topological group that is not totally disconnected, do the four separable quotient variants all hold: existence of a non-trivial separable quotient group, existence of an infinite separable quotient group, existence of a separable metrizable quotient group, and existence of an infinite separable metrizable quotient group?

evidence.quote: Does every infinite non-totally disconnected locally compact group have a separable quotient group which is (i) non-trivial; (ii) infinite; (iii) metrizable; (iv) infinite metrizable?

accepted.question_text: For every infinite reflexive abelian topological group G, where reflexive means that the natural map from G into its second dual group is a topological group isomorphism, do the four separable quotient variants all hold: existence of a non-trivial separable quotient group, existence of an infinite separable quotient group, existence of a separable metrizable quotient group, and existence of an infinite separable metrizable quotient group?

evidence.quote: Recall that an abelian topological group G is called a reflexive topological group if the natural map of G into its second dual group is a topological group isomorphism.
Does every infinite reflexive abelian topological group, G, have a separable quotient group which is (i) non-trivial; (ii) infinite; (iii) metrizable; (iv) infinite metrizable?

accepted.question_text: Can one construct a precompact abelian topological group G whose quotient groups are all either trivial or non-separable, as in the known zero-dimensional dense subgroup example of T^c, and which additionally has at least one of the following properties: G is connected, G is a Baire space, or G is reflexive?

evidence.quote: There exists an uncountable dense subgroup G of the compact group T^c satisfying dimG=0 such that every countable subgroup of G is closed in G and every uncountable subgroup of G is dense in G. Hence every quotient group of G is either trivial or non-separable.
Does there exist a precompact abelian group G as in Theorem 36 which has one of the following additional properties: (a) G is connected; (b) G is Baire; (c) G is reflexive?

accepted.question_text: For every Tychonoff space X and every infinite subspace S of the closed unit interval [0,1], does the free abelian topological group A(X) admit an open continuous homomorphism onto the free abelian topological group A(S)?

evidence.quote: Let, as usual, F(X) and A(X) denote the free topological group and the free abelian topological group of a Tychonoff space X, respectively.
Does there exist an open continuous homomorphism of A(X) onto A(S), where X is an arbitrary Tychonoff space and S is an infinite subspace of the closed unit interval [0,1]?

accepted.question_text: For every Lindelof space X and every infinite space Y with a countable network, does the free abelian topological group A(X) admit an open continuous homomorphism onto the free abelian topological group A(Y)?
accepted.context_brief: free abelian quotients with countable networks

evidence.quote: Does there exist an open continuous homomorphism of A(X) onto A(Y), where X is an arbitrary Lindelof space and Y is an infinite space which has a countable network?

Likely open-question regions were Sections 2.5, 3.2, 3.4, 4.3, 4.5, 5, 5.4, and 6.4.

Extracted the implicit Remark 3 question and Problems 5-9 on S-separable groups, product permanence, ZFC status of counterexamples, and C_p(X).

Extracted Problems 10-18 on separable quotient problems for Banach spaces, general topological groups, locally compact groups, reflexive abelian groups, and precompact abelian groups without separable quotients.
